page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-48 is an x86_64 compute instance offering 48 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of system memory. Designed with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration allocates 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This specification places processing throughput ahead of memory capacity, supporting applications that require high parallel CPU capacity without the operational cost of surplus memory allocation.

The n4d-highcpu-48 includes no bundled local storage, requiring external persistent disk volumes to support file systems and persistent storage workloads. Furthermore, the instance provides zero GPU accelerators and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Network topology and remote volume configuration must be provisioned independently.

The qualitative efficiency profile of this instance favors compute-dense processing. Deployments that run heavy multi-threaded calculations or high-throughput batch operations maximize hardware resource utilization. It is appropriate for software build compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, video transcoding, and CPU-intensive distributed microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused x86_64 server instance configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of total system memory. Featuring a compact 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, this instance targets environments where parallel processing density is prioritized over expansive memory allocations. The instance includes no bundled local storage, meaning all persistent file systems must rely on network-attached storage infrastructure. Additionally, the instance provides zero GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The cost efficiency profile favors compute-intensive scenarios that scale horizontally across high thread counts without spending resources on unused RAM. Consequently, the n4d-highcpu-48 is designed for CPU-bound applications, including distributed batch processing, automated software compilation, media transcoding, and continuous integration and deployment pipelines.
